newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish farmers pelt French embassy with tomatoes.
newsitem.headline: Spanish farmers pelt French embassy with tomatoes.

text.p: Spanish farmers pelted the French embassy in Madrid with tomatoes and eggs on Saturday to protest against attacks on Spanish truckers importing vegetables and fruits to France.
About 100 angry farmers armed with 9,000 kilograms of tomatoes and 100 dozen eggs hurled some of the food at the embassy but after police intervened, they dumped the rest at the building entrance.

"We want to say here, at the house of the representatives of the French farmers, we are fed up with the insults and the robbery which we have suffered for more than 10 years," said Pedro Barato, president of the farmers association ASAJA which organised the demonstration.
"...If the aggression continues, we are not going to remain with our arms folded," he added.

Over the past week, French farmers who want tighter controls on fruit and vegetable imports have been stopping incoming Spanish trucks to dump and burn their loads. They have also raided warehouses and destroyed imported produce.

Spanish television broadcast on Saturday pictures of some 400 French farmers raiding a warehouse full of imported food near Marseille overnight and said its contents were completely destroyed. It said such attacks were an annual occurrence.
Madrid has accused French authorities of turning a blind eye to the attacks and has sought European Union action to penalise its northern neighbour.

The French have apologised and President Jacques Chirac assured Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar on Friday at the European Union summit in Noordwijk, Holland that he would try to prevent further violence.
Spanish farmers have urged the government to press for the suspension of all EU aid to the French agricultural sector. They have also called on Spaniards to boycott all French products.
